name: PinguinoSpotify
desc: Spotify queue you own: drag-to-reorder, viewer song requests (!sr, !skip), fair ordering, stream-safe mode, OBS now-playing overlay.

help.title: SPOTIFY_API_KEY
help.summary: A shared password between this PC and innocentpenguin.com so the site can trust the module. You make it up; it is not a Spotify key.
steps: Make a random value of 32 or more characters (a password manager can generate one).
Paste it in Railway > your site service > Variables as SPOTIFY_API_KEY.
Paste the same value here with Set, then press Test (it must say OK).
To rotate: change both places to a new value.
help.example: 32+ random letters and digits (format only; never share the real value)

_module.title: PinguinoSpotify
_module.summary: A Spotify queue you own: reorder it, let viewers request songs, and show what is playing on stream.
steps: One-time: create a free Spotify developer app and connect it on the Spotify page (Setup tab). Needs Spotify Premium.
Open Spotify on the streaming PC and press play once so a playback device exists.
Add songs in Search, or let viewers use !sr in chat. Drag rows to reorder; only the next song is sent to Spotify, shortly before the current one ends.
Song requests ship CLOSED. Open them with the toggle on the Queue tab, '!sr open' in chat, or the site's mod page.
OBS: add a Browser source with http://127.0.0.1:8771/overlay, or a Text source reading Data\runtime\spotify\nowplaying.txt.
Website link (optional): set the site URL on the Setup tab and SPOTIFY_API_KEY in Integrations > Key vault.
To redo setup: Setup tab > Disconnect, then Connect again.

token.title: Spotify connected
token.summary: The module needs a Spotify login (a Client ID from your developer app, then one approval in the browser) to read and control playback.
steps: Open the Spotify developer dashboard and press Create app (any name, choose Web API).
In the app's settings add the Redirect URI exactly: http://127.0.0.1:8771/callback (the literal 127.0.0.1, not localhost) and save.
Copy the app's Client ID (no client secret is needed) and paste it on the Spotify page > Setup tab, then press Save.
Press Connect to Spotify, approve in the browser window that opens, then come back.
If it says login failed or the token was rejected, press Disconnect and Connect again. A changed Spotify password or 'remove access' on spotify.com/account/apps also needs a new Connect.
When green: the login is stored on this PC and refreshes itself; nothing more to do.
token.example: Client ID format: 32 letters and digits, e.g. 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

premium.title: Spotify Premium
premium.summary: Spotify only lets apps control playback (skip, queue, play) for Premium accounts.
steps: Check that the account you connected is the Premium one (the Spotify page shows its name after connecting).
If it is a Free account, upgrade at spotify.com/premium, or Disconnect and Connect again with the Premium account.
Without Premium the queue page and chat commands still load but playback control fails.
When green: the connected account is Premium.

device.title: Active Spotify device
device.summary: Spotify needs a running player (the desktop app on the streaming PC) before the module can queue or skip.
steps: Open the Spotify desktop app on the streaming PC and sign in with the connected account.
Press play on any song once, then pause if you like. This makes the PC an active device.
If several devices are listed, pick the PC in the device dropdown on the Spotify page.
Make sure Spotify is not set to private/silent mode on another device that took over playback.
When green: the named device is active and the module can control it.

api.title: Spotify reachable
api.summary: The module could not talk to Spotify's servers just now.
steps: Check the PC's internet connection.
Look at the Console for 'auth' or 'api' lines from the spotify module; a repeated rate-limit message means Spotify asked us to slow down and it recovers by itself.
If it keeps failing, open the Spotify page > Setup and press Disconnect, then Connect.
When green: Spotify answers normally.

requests.title: Song requests open/closed
requests.summary: Viewer requests ship CLOSED. This shows the current state; closed is normal when you are not taking requests.
steps: Open requests: toggle 'requests open' on the Queue tab, type '!sr open' in chat as a mod, or use open on the site's /mod/music page.
Close them with the same controls ('!sr close').
Rules (limits, explicit filter, blocklist, approval inbox, stream-safe mode) are on the Settings tab.
Stream-safe mode blocks explicit songs and holds every request in the Requests tab until you approve it.
The chat commands must also be enabled on the Host's Actions & Events page (they ship disabled), with Nightbot's !sr turned off.
requests.example: !sr open   !sr close   !sr never gonna give you up

site.title: Website link (innocentpenguin.com)
site.summary: Optional: the PC sends now-playing and the queue to the site and receives viewer requests from it. The PC is never exposed; it only calls out.
steps: Set the same SPOTIFY_API_KEY in Railway Variables (32+ characters; site side) and in Integrations > Key vault (this PC). Also set SPOTIFY_CLIENT_ID and SPOTIFY_CLIENT_SECRET in Railway (a Spotify developer app, client credentials only).
On the Spotify page > Setup > Website, enter https://innocentpenguin.com and tick enabled.
Use Test next to the key in Integrations to check the site accepts it. A 401 means the two keys differ.
If the site is down the module keeps working locally and retries automatically (3 s up to 30 s).
When green: the site shows your now-playing and queue at /music.

voice_skip.title: Voice skip
voice_skip.summary: Saying 'skip' to the Voice bot skips the current song, even while requests are closed. Nothing is posted to chat.
steps: The Voice bot sends POST /api/chat-command {command: skip, role: broadcaster, silent: true} to this module.
It works whenever Spotify is playing; the skip is logged in the Console with source 'voice'.
If nothing happens, check the Spotify item above is green and a device is active.
